question: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Gross margin (GAAP))

calls.reasoning: On the Q2 FY27 call (Aug 26, 2026) NVIDIA said gross margin would be 74% in Q3 then fall to 71-72% in Q4 FY27 due to memory cost inflation, recovering to 72-73% in FY28 via price increases. The formal Q4 guide (Q3 release, ~Nov 2026) should land near that pre-announced 71.5% midpoint; GAAP and non-GAAP were guided equal for Q3. Upside risk: earlier price increases or easing memory; downside: further memory inflation or Rubin ramp costs. Small tails for one-off charges. Markets: only Polymarket markets on actual Q3 adjusted GM (73-75% at 0.81, thin volume) - a different contract (Q3 actuals, non-GAAP), used only as a check that Q3 is tracking ~74%; no market on Q4 guidance found.
calls.dossier:
- Q2 FY27 press release (Aug 26, 2026, nvidianews/SEC 8-K): Q2 revenue $96.2B, GAAP & non-GAAP GM 75.0%. Q3 outlook: revenue $108.0B +/-2%, GAAP and non-GAAP GM 74.0% +/-50bp, opex $9.2B GAAP / $9.0B non-GAAP. Release Outlook section contains NO Q4 GM statement.
- Earnings call / press coverage (The Elec, Aug 27, 2026; TIKR; gamesreviews headline 'Q4 FY27 71-72%'): management said GM expected 74% in Q3 and to 'fall to 71% to 72% in the fourth quarter' (Nov-Jan), 'bottom' there, then recover to 72-73% in FY2028 as price increases begin in FY28.
- Cause: memory price increases exceeded prior expectations and are 'headed higher into next year' (Kress); purchase commitments rose from $119B to $279B, mostly memory.
- Vera Rubin began shipping Aug 2026, expected ~20% of Q3 data center revenue (new-product ramp historically margin-dilutive).
- History: Q4 FY26 guide GAAP 74.8%/non-GAAP 75.0%; actual GAAP 75.0%. Recent quarters GAAP and non-GAAP guided equal or within 0.2pt.
- Prior FY27 target had been 'mid-70s' exit; the Aug call lowered it.
- Status quo: formal Q4 guide matches the pre-announced 71-72% band (midpoint 71.5).
- Resolves off the Outlook section of the Q3 FY27 press release (GAAP GM midpoint, rounded to 0.1%), not the call commentary or non-GAAP figure.
- Event window: Q3 FY27 release expected ~Nov 18-19, 2026 (question scheduled resolution Nov 17); as of Oct 25, 2026 the guide is not yet issued.
- Markets: Polymarket only has Q3 actual adjusted GM bucket markets (different contract).
- Searched but not found: any October 2026 update to memory pricing impact, analyst consensus for Q4 GM guide.

calls.reasoning: On the Q2 FY27 call (Aug 26, 2026) CFO Kress said gross margin would bottom in Q4 FY27 at 71-72% because of extreme memory pricing, after a 74.0% ±50bp Q3 guide (Q2 actual was 75.0%). NVIDIA's next-quarter guides have historically come in on its earlier forward margin comments (e.g. 'mid-70s by year end' became a 74.8% Q4 FY26 GAAP guide). That makes a 71.5% midpoint modal, with 71.0% and 72.0% next. Downside: memory costs already beat expectations and Rubin ramps in Q4. Upside: price increases already taken and a possible Q3 beat. No market on the Q4 guide was found; Polymarket's Q3 actual non-GAAP GM markets (73-75% at 0.81, thin volume) are consistent with Q3 landing near guidance.

calls.reasoning: On the Q2 FY27 call (Aug 26, 2026) CFO Kress said gross margin bottoms in Q4 FY27 at 71-72% because of memory cost inflation, after a 74.0% ±50bp Q3 guide. NVIDIA's point ±50bp guides have historically matched its earlier verbal margin comments, so the Q4 GAAP midpoint should be 71.0-72.0, most likely 71.5. Slight downside lean: memory prices are still rising and GAAP can run 0.1pt below non-GAAP. Upside: price increases already taken. Small tails priced for one-off charges or a regime change. Markets: Polymarket only prices Q3 actual non-GAAP GM (73-75% at 0.81, thin volume), a different contract, so it is a consistency check only; no market on the Q4 guide was found.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: the 71-72% Q4 bottom comment, the 74.0% Q3 guide, the formal guide not yet issued as of 2026-10-25, and no matching market. The only factual gap is whether GAAP will be guided equal to non-GAAP (recent quarters, including Q3) or 0.1pt lower (Q1 FY27); the dossiers can't settle it, so I tilt slightly downward. Risk skew is a judgment call; I lean slightly downward because memory costs have already exceeded NVIDIA's expectations. I agree with and carry forward the runs' shared reference class and ~1.3-1.4 dispersion. No web retrieval was done on this run.
